To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the eigenspectrum is robust to sparsification/entry-wise nonlinear transformations; and (2) this implies that downstream spectral clustering is robust to sparsity and quantization.

(a) sparse quantized spectral clustering (SQC) is a powerful technique that allows one to speed up the computation and reduce the memory requirements of spectral clustering by a factor proportional to the sparsity level of the matrix, (b) the spectral clustering performance of the sparse quantized matrix is essentially the same as the spectral clustering performance on the dense original matrix, and (c) the sparse quantized spectral embedding is essentially the same (in a spectral norm sense) as the dense original spectral embedding

(1) sparsification and quantization do not significantly alter the eigenstructure of a matrix and (2) sparsification/ quantization of the input matrix does not significantly alter the performance of spectral clustering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how does a matrix's eigenstructure change under sparsity-inducing and quantization-inducing operations?
understanding the impact of nonlinear entry-wise transformations on spectral clustering.
the question: how does the eigenspectrum change under nonlinear transformations?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the eigenspectrum is a robust invariant under sparsification, quantization, or other entry-wise nonlinear transformations.
sparse quantized spectral clustering is an effective way to speed up spectral clustering.

sparse quantized spectral clustering is a robust and effective approach to clustering large datasets, even when the sparsification/ quantization rate is very high, and even when the underlying data matrix is very ill-conditioned.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can now perform sparse and quantized spectral clustering with no loss in performance, while enjoying the benefits of sparsity and quantization.
the spectral clustering problem can be solved very efficiently and robustly with respect to data sparsification and quantization.

, in the context of spectral clustering, sparsifying and quantizing can be done with very little downstream loss in accuracy, and in fact can be used to speed up the algorithm and/or reduce the storage footprint.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for many practical problems, it is possible to work with much more sparse or quantized data than previously thought, and still obtain accurate results.

, when working with large data matrices, one can afford to aggressively sparsify/quantize them, without incurring significant downstream performance loss, and without needing to know the exact sparsity pattern or the exact quantization scheme.
, for many applications in which spectral clustering is used, it is possible to dramatically reduce the storage and computational requirements without sacrificing performance.
